SNOT KLAP SPORT PROPOSAL

Title: Power Slap: South Africa's Danie van Heerden Aims for Global Glory

Power Slap is an emerging sport that has captivated audiences worldwide with its raw intensity and spectacle. Originating in 2022, this competition has quickly gained traction, and on June 28th, it will feature a significant contender: South African heavyweight Danie "Pitbull" van Heerden.

The Rise of Power Slap , founded by Ultimate Fighting Championship UFC President Dana White, involves two competitors taking turns slapping each other with an open hand. Matches are decided through a combination of knockouts and judge scoring based on slap effectiveness and the opponent's reaction. The sport is both controversial and thrilling, drawing significant attention and debate about its legitimacy and safety.

Danie van Heerden, hailing from Pretoria, South Africa, is a notable figure in Power Slap. Previously a boxer and wrestler, van Heerden transitioned to Power Slap after witnessing its debut in South Africa in 2022. Overcoming personal tragedies, including the loss of his father and battles with mental health, van Heerden has found new purpose and success in this sport. His story is one of resilience and determination, symbolized by his nickname "Pitbull."

A Power Slap match begins with a coin toss to decide who strikes first. The first striker has 60 seconds to deliver a slap, which must be open-handed and connect below the eye and above the chin. Opponents cannot flinch or defend themselves and have 60 seconds to recover. Matches typically last three rounds unless a knockout occurs, with judges scoring based on the slap's impact and the opponent's response.

While the spectacle of Power Slap is undeniable, the sport raises significant concerns about brain health. Repeated slaps to the head can lead to traumatic brain injuries (TBI), concussions, and long-term neurological issues. Neurologists have emphasized that any sport involving blows to the head poses serious risks. Symptoms such as memory loss, cognitive decline, and emotional instability can result from the brain's repeated trauma. Dana White, who has championed the sport, argues that in a boxing match a fighter will typically receive about 300 blows, which is a lot less than the 3 hits in Power Slap.
Competitors like van Heerden are aware of these risks but are drawn to the sport's challenge and the potential rewards. For each performance Danie receives R 90 000, much more than he has ever earned in any other sport. Despite the professional oversight and safety measures in place, the inherent danger remains, prompting ongoing debates about the ethical implications of Power Slap.

van Heerden aims to become South Africa’s first world Power Slap champion on June 28th. (He did not take the title.)

Power Slap is a controversial yet fascinating sport that has found a global audience. South Africa's Danie van Heerden is at the forefront of this movement, bringing his resilience and determination to the international stage. While the sport's future and safety remain topics of intense discussion, van Heerden's journey is a testament to the power of human spirit and the pursuit of greatness against all odds.

Snot Klap Rough




V/O
[churchbells] Many of his neighbours are at church, but Johan’s mind is elsewhere.

[CUTAWAY TO SLAP]

He’s gearing up for a contest of strength and endurance…

[CUTAWAY TO SLAP]

Johan: The nerves are always there. But you know, I’ve got this one.

[CUTAWAY TO SLAP]

…he’s hoping to hit the bigtime in the latest global combat sports phenomenon.

Johan
It’s for me and escape

[VISUAL SEQUENCE OF SLAPS TO SEGUE AND BUILD UP INTO INTRO]

VO

As controversial as it is captivating, slap fighting is watched by an audience of millions. And we're taking you into the heat of the action..."

Johan: When he hit me, my brain crashed against my skull, and for a moment all I saw was white..

VO: …and former boxer and martial arts champion Danie van Heerden…

Danie: I know that South Africans are the only ones who know how to give a good …klap.

VO: And one of the main pioneers, Agisanang Ramarutsi.

Agi: Once the slap goes it's universal. You know, that guy got slapped, you know he's in pain. How is he going to handle that?

VO

Slap fighting is a combat sport. Two combatants take turns to slap each other in the face with an open hand. The objective is to deliver a massive “snotklap” or blow to your opponent’s unprotected head that leaves them unconscious.

It started as a viral phenomenon in Russia around 2019 - attracting both men and women.

It’s a brand new sport, so most competitors have a former life. [visuals of Johan as a boxer]

Lourensa

OK. How did you go from boxing to power slapping?

Johan

A friend on TikTok said to me, “Johan, my opponent withdrew from the slap fighting competition. You are a boxer, come and hit me.”

And I said “You guys are crazy! Who hits each other?”


And eventually I said I will do it and tick it off my bucket list.


And I was the first one in South Africa to break someone’s jaw with an open hit.

Lourensa
So, the bug bit you immediately?

Johan
The bug bit instantly.

V/O
Today, Johan is on the draw card for a big event on the SA Slap Fighting Association calendar: Thunderstruck.

[behind the scenes and maybe an upsound from prep? Build up to the big moment]

He is up against Shaun “NoisyBoy” Gerber, who has lost all 4 of his previous fights…but is still hooked on the sport.

Lourensa


Why do you think people are so fascinated by the sport?

Shaun

In boxing and MMA there is a lot of skill and training involved and you learn how to avoid the shots. In this sport, you stand in front of your opponent and say give me your best shot and I will give you mine.


V/O

While Johan and Shaun prepare backstage, Danie van Heerden explains the rules to the audience.

UPS
Danie
Keep in mind, no palm strike, no cupping, no fingers back.

V/O
The rules are quite simple, there are judges, paramedics and body catchers.
• No slaps to the temple, neck, or under jaw
• No flinching or ducking
• And you get 60 seconds to recover

UPS
Guys good luck
Sportmanship
We are on Carte Blanche

V/O
Danie’s father was a professional boxer and he coached his son in the ring. Danie competed in various martial arts for 11 years, but he made his slap fighting debut two years ago. His very first slap floored his opponent.

Danie
He was probably out for nine minutes or so and then I'm hooked.

V/O
His second fight was less successful…

Danie
He slapped me so hard. I was on a two-week liquid diet, I couldn't eat, my jaw stood like this.

UPS SOUND EINAAH

But a viral video started from there and we had 17.6 million views and then Power Slap contacted me.

V/O
And with that Danie hit the big time, fighting for Power Slap in the official American slap fighting league. He is currently ranked third worldwide in the super heavy-weight division.

Lourensa
And how has that been for you?

Danie

Life changing. I've made more money in eight months, which I've made 11 years of combat sports.

VO
Agi Ramarutsi may have been one of the first pioneers of slap fighting in South Africa, introducing it to Kagiso, west of Johannesburg, after seeing a match on social media four years ago.

Agi

My first introduction was during COVID…then I was like, oh, this seems like something that you could appreciate. So I was like, hey, why not bring it here? You know? And ever since then, it's been a crazy ride.


V/O

Agi roped in a small crowd to watch his first fight against his friend B.I.G, who’s almost twice his size.

Agi

B.I.G. hit me and I fell out of the frame.

And you can see by the crowd reaction that something great had started.
And I said I am going to push this and make it what it needs to be.

V/O
And so Elite Slap Sports was born. In just two years, it’s drawn an impressive following, with over 15 million views on some online videos.
Agi

This to the hood is something else.

UPS
Ladies and gentlemen, our first fight this afternoon.

V/O

At Chicago Piano Bar, the first slap fight is underway.


Lourensa

00:28:56:05 - 00:28:59:14
Why are people so interested in watching people slap each other?


Danie
So I think this is a quicker sports for a knockout that everyone want to see. And knocking doesn't matter what they want, it's what they say. They want to see a knockout.

Lourensa

But if the aim of the game is to cause a knockout and essentially head injuries, it's not barbaric.


Danie

Doesn't matter what you want to do, the pros and cons
towards everything. It's like smoking.

It's bad for you. Yeah, but you do it. It's okay. So that fight I do it and you watch it. So yeah.

V/O
The early fights done, it's time for Johan and Shaun to face off.

Johan

It’s the first time in slap fighting that I have felt my brain basically hitting my skull.

I think I saw for a moment my
grandmother who is not with us anymore.

I almost thought, I wouldn’t recover from the blow.

Sean

I knew that I had hurt him after that first hit. You feel sorry for your opponent, but it is a sport and you go in for the kill.

V/O
It's evident that Johan is disoriented by the hit.
VO
And that’s what makes slap fighting as controversial as it is popular. A hard blow to the head can bounce the brain around inside the skull, causing injuries that can affect brain function.

It's an injury sometimes seen in other contact sports like rugby.



Lourensa link


Concussion is a major concern in rugby, but the injury is usually unintentional. Slap fighting is on a whole different playing field where the intention is to cause head trauma.

V/O
So we asked Dr. Rob Collins, the concussion physician for the Lions Rugby Company, to take a look at Johan’s fight.

Rob

He staggers there which equals a criteria 1 concussion. In rugby if you stagger like that after a knock you don’t qualify for a head assessment you are removed from play immediately.

V/O

That rugby player would not be allowed to play for the next 21 days.

But, it’s the repeated untreated concussions that can cause irreversible brain damage.



Rob
So you get repeated bruises to the brain, it will cause a scar and scares affect the function of the brain.

V/O
Johan flinches. He's disqualified and Shaun secures his first ever slap fight win.

Lourensa

Do you have long term health concerns?


Danie

To be honest, no. I mean I've been doing this for two years now. I've taken 11 blows to my head, which in my 11 years of combat sports, I'll probably take maybe a million blows played. But for me to get a better life for my kids and to open it up for South Africa I would take that chance.

V/O
Whether you think it is a sport or just a spectacle, its massive appeal is undeniable, There is no doubt of its dangers. But those who take part say “ If you don’t like it, don’t watch it.”



THE END

Enter the arena of slap fighting, the latest combat sport, where the stakes are high and every hit counts. It is a sport or a spectacle?

Danie
This is the only sport where you can go and watch for 5 minuets and you will definitely see a knock out.

No 3
From local bars to international fame, slap fighting is taking the world by storm.

metadata.Further information: SNOT KLAP SPORT PROPOSAL Title: Power Slap: South Africa's Danie van Heerden Aims for Global Glory Power Slap is an emerging sport that has captivated audiences worldwide with its raw intensity and spectacle. Originating in 2022, this competition has quickly gained traction, and on June 28th, it will feature a significant contender: South African heavyweight Danie "Pitbull" van Heerden. The Rise of Power Slap , founded by Ultimate Fighting Championship UFC President Dana White, involves two competitors taking turns slapping each other with an open hand. Matches are decided through a combination of knockouts and judge scoring based on slap effectiveness and the opponent's reaction. The sport is both controversial and thrilling, drawing significant attention and debate about its legitimacy and safety. Danie van Heerden, hailing from Pretoria, South Africa, is a notable figure in Power Slap. Previously a boxer and wrestler, van Heerden transitioned to Power Slap after witnessing its debut in South Africa in 2022. Overcoming personal tragedies, including the loss of his father and battles with mental health, van Heerden has found new purpose and success in this sport. His story is one of resilience and determination, symbolized by his nickname "Pitbull." A Power Slap match begins with a coin toss to decide who strikes first. The first striker has 60 seconds to deliver a slap, which must be open-handed and connect below the eye and above the chin. Opponents cannot flinch or defend themselves and have 60 seconds to recover. Matches typically last three rounds unless a knockout occurs, with judges scoring based on the slap's impact and the opponent's response. While the spectacle of Power Slap is undeniable, the sport raises significant concerns about brain health. Repeated slaps to the head can lead to traumatic brain injuries (TBI), concussions, and long-term neurological issues. Neurologists have emphasized that any sport involving blows to the head poses serious risks. Symptoms such as memory loss, cognitive decline, and emotional instability can result from the brain's repeated trauma. Dana White, who has championed the sport, argues that in a boxing match a fighter will typically receive about 300 blows, which is a lot less than the 3 hits in Power Slap. Competitors like van Heerden are aware of these risks but are drawn to the sport's challenge and the potential rewards. For each performance Danie receives R 90 000, much more than he has ever earned in any other sport. Despite the professional oversight and safety measures in place, the inherent danger remains, prompting ongoing debates about the ethical implications of Power Slap. van Heerden aims to become South Africa’s first world Power Slap champion on June 28th. (He did not take the title.) Power Slap is a controversial yet fascinating sport that has found a global audience. South Africa's Danie van Heerden is at the forefront of this movement, bringing his resilience and determination to the international stage. While the sport's future and safety remain topics of intense discussion, van Heerden's journey is a testament to the power of human spirit and the pursuit of greatness against all odds.
